findings.decompiled: mem[... + 160 len 4] = 157198259 / if ext_code.size(fundsAsset): idx = 0 / while idx < 68: mem[idx + ... + 228] = mem[idx + ...] ... / call fundsAsset with: gas gas_remaining args mem[... + 228 len 68]
findings.source: ERC20Helper.approve(fundsAsset, loan, amount) -> _call(token_, abi.encodeWithSelector(IERC20Like.approve.selector, spender_, amount_)): token_.code.length == 0 ? false : token_.call(data_), then abi.decode(returnData, (bool)) when returnData.length > 0
findings.issue: The 68-byte call data built by abi.encodeWithSelector is copied by a while with a constant bound (P7) and the call keeps raw-memory arguments without a name (P2), with the approve/transfer selector printed in decimal (157198259 = 0x095ea7b3, 13 lines).
findings.rule: A word loop copying a constant n bytes is the copy line mem[d len n] = mem[s len n] (here unrolled to three words); once copied, a call on mem[d len 68] whose first 4 bytes are a constant selector is named and its two words printed as arguments.

findings.function: fund(address) and the functions that make many calls before a transfer
findings.source: successive external calls (unoptimised build: each call's returndata advances the free-memory pointer)
findings.issue: The free-memory pointer, known as a sum of ten ceil32(return_data.size) terms, is spelled out in every memory address (41 lines, most cut at 240 characters), which hides the few words actually stored.
findings.rule: Bind a symbolic free-memory pointer value to one name when it is first read (p = mem[64]) and print addresses as p + k.

notes: No explicit loop in the reached source (the ERC20Helper and loan accounting are loop-free). The 15 whiles are implicit: the constant 68-byte call-data copies of _call (P7), bytes copies for the low-level call and revert data, and the ABI decoding of the bytes[] calls parameter of rejectNewTerms/proposeNewTerms. Unoptimised build: repeated scratch writes (P8). claim (910 pack lines) and the two triggerDefault variants reviewed by structure (calls, events, storage writes, reverts with their LM: messages); the rest line by line.
summary: Faithful and loop-free in the source; readability suffers from low-level ERC20 calls left as raw memory after constant-length copy loops and from free-memory addresses spelled as long sums.
